What is the Italian 2002 Mole one cent coin worth?

25 November 20262 min read

Short answer

In 2013 Bolaffi put a used Italian Mole cent at around €1,500. The rare error has a 1 on the common side and the Mole tower on the national side.

In this article

  1. Read the number and measure the coin
  2. Follow the figures back to the sale
  3. A find worth having examined
  4. Check it yourself

You tip an old jar of copper coins onto the table and notice a tall tower on an Italian piece. Turn it over. If you see a 1 on the other side and the coin is dated 2002, you have the first clues to the Italian Mole cent error. Auction house Bolaffi put a used example at about €1,500 in 2013.

The tower is the Mole Antonelliana, the design used on Italy’s regular 2 cent. The sought-after error pairs that design with the common face of a one cent coin. The size matters too, which is why a picture of the tower on its own gives you an incomplete identification.

Read the number and measure the coin

Start with the large 1 on the common face. The regular Italian one cent design on the other side is Castel del Monte. The error shows the Mole tower there instead. The date should read 2002, and the piece measures 18.75 millimetres across. That is the size of a 2 cent coin.

A regular Italian 2 cent makes a useful comparison for the picture and diameter. Set one next to your find and turn both coins over to check the number on the common side. The tower is part of the ordinary design on the 2 cent, so the denomination on the side opposite the tower is what makes this particular match interesting.

Follow the figures back to the sale

Bolaffi sold an example on 23 May 2013 for €6,600 including costs, from a starting price of €2,500. Later auction figures reported for around 2015 were nearer €2,500. The €2,500 to €6,600 range for uncirculated pieces is based on historical figures. Recent prices are unavailable.

Bolaffi’s figure of about €1,500 for a used coin is a separate historical estimate. That is the figure to look at if you are trying to put a worn example in context. The auction figure has its own sale history and applies to a different example.

A find worth having examined

Estimates of the original mintage differ, and only a few dozen examples have been found. The error is easy to fake, which matters as soon as you have a piece with matching designs, date and size. A physical examination is worth arranging. A coin with a known provenance or an assessment is easier to sell than a piece whose history and authenticity are uncertain.

Check it yourself

Put your coins on a table and take a photo with Euroreveal. The app helps identify the coin and shows what it could be worth.

The Mole Antonelliana design makes an ordinary Italian 2 cent coin a mint error.

Show the answer

False. The tower belongs on the regular 2 cent. The error is a 2002 Italian one cent coin carrying that design.
